case_title: Pradeep Kumar v. State of Haryana
weapon: Kerosene used to set the victim on fire; no weapon mentioned
evidence_type: Dying declaration; medical (post-mortem) evidence; oral testimony of mother and father; magistrate's testimony; letter from victim to father
aggravating_circumstances: Death by burns within nine months of marriage; soon-before-death cruelty and harassment over dowry demand
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.498-A and s.304-B by Sessions Judge, Kamal (judgment 1 August 1997); sentence amount not stated
high_court_outcome: Revision/appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence affirmed (judgment 3 February 2010)
offence_finally_established: Dowry death under IPC s.304-B; cruelty/harassment under IPC s.498-A
neutral_facts: The victim was married to the accused on 20 June 1995. On 1 March 1996, about nine months after the marriage, she suffered burn injuries. Her statement, recorded by a Chief Judicial Magistrate on 2 March 1996 after a medical fitness endorsement, had two parts. The first part described an accident in which a kerosene stove burst while she was preparing tea. The second part alleged that the accused had been pressing her to bring Rs. One lakh from her parents and had threatened to kill her. It further alleged that the accused had tried to hang her, had earlier tried to burn her at night, and at about 5.30 a.m. had doused her from behind with kerosene and set her alight. She stated that the first part had been tutored by the accused. A First Information Report was registered on the basis of that statement. The victim died on 12 March 1996. The post-mortem examination found superficial to deep burns over most of the body, excluding the face, scalp, both legs, feet and part of the left upper arm. The doctor recorded that the cause of death was ante mortem burns. He agreed that kerosene poured from behind would leave burns on the back, and that a stove burst would ordinarily have affected the face and scalp, which were not burnt. The victim's mother testified that the victim had told her of quarrels over a demand of Rs. One lakh for a piggery farm. The victim's father testified to the same demand and to physical abuse. A letter from the victim to her father demanding Rs. 5,000 was also in evidence. The accused was reported to have donated blood, but the victim died despite it. The case was then converted to a dowry-related offence and a charge sheet was filed.
offence_severity: Maximum: imprisonment for life; Minimum: seven years imprisonment (IPC s.304-B). For s.498-A the judgment states imprisonment up to three years and fine.
physical_harm: Superficial to deep burns over most of the body; death from ante mortem burns on 12 March 1996
premeditation_planning: Not stated; the court recorded the dying declaration's account of an earlier night-time attempt but made no express finding of premeditation
motive: Demand for dowry of Rs. One lakh (for piggery farm) from the victim's parents, with harassment and threats to force compliance; accepted by the court
key_evidence_accepted: Second part of the dying declaration; evidence of the victim's father (PW-8); post-mortem evidence (PW-7) that burns were ante mortem; mother's (PW-6) evidence of dowry demand
witness_credibility: Court accepted the father's evidence and the second part of the dying declaration as reliable; the first part was found tutored by the accused
post_offence_conduct: Not stated (court did not separately find post-offence conduct; the prosecution case alleged the accused tried to save her)
bail_history: Not stated; Supreme Court cancelled the bail bond
trial_duration: offence: 1 March 1996 (burn injuries; death 12 March 1996); trial judgment: 1 August 1997; High Court: 3 February 2010; Supreme Court: 2 July 2014
legal_representation: Appellant: K. K. Mohan; Respondent (State): Anil Kaushik and Kamal Mohan Gupta
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; case converted to s.304-B; charge sheet presented and accused committed for trial
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted (s.498-A and s.304-B). High Court: dismissed, conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
defence_argument: Medical evidence contradicts the prosecution story; the occurrence was an accident from a bursting kerosene stove; the dying declaration cannot be relied upon because its first part contradicts the second
legal_principle_applied: Essentials for s.304-B and presumption under s.113-B Evidence Act; dying declaration accepted in part (second part reliable, first part tutored)
precedent_relied_upon: Hira Lal & Ors. v. State (Govt. of NCT), Delhi (2003) 8 SCC 80
judicial_aggravating_factors: Death by burns within nine months of marriage, preceded by dowry-related cruelty and harassment
other_sentence_order: Bail bond cancelled; accused directed to be taken into custody to serve the remainder of sentence
